grade_crosswalk.manuscript_definition: Individual-level cohort with cancer outcomes, dose/exposure reconstruction, adequate latency, confounder control
grade_crosswalk.GRADE_certainty: Moderate-High (well-conducted cohort; upgradeable for dose-response/large effect)
grade_crosswalk.BradfordHill_typically_satisfied: Strength; temporality; dose-response; biological plausibility; consistency
grade_crosswalk.notes: Observational starts Low in GRADE but upgrades on dose-response + confounder control (e.g. LSS).

grade_crosswalk.manuscript_definition: Cohort or registry study with defined exposed and comparison groups but incomplete smoking or exposure data
grade_crosswalk.notes: Downgraded for residual confounding / exposure misclassification.

grade_crosswalk.manuscript_definition: Biomarker, cytogenetic, or mechanistic evidence linked to an exposed population
grade_crosswalk.notes: Maps to the mechanistic evidence stream in OHAT/GRADE, not the effect body.

grade_crosswalk.manuscript_definition: Community survey, thesis, early-disaster follow-up, or immature-latency cohort
grade_crosswalk.notes: Excluded from the effect body in OHAT/Navigation Guide; retained here as flagged signal.

grade_crosswalk.manuscript_definition: Legal or policy presumption based on evidence review
grade_crosswalk.NavigationGuide_strength: Out of scope (policy, not toxicity evidence)
grade_crosswalk.OHAT_confidence_and_hazard: Out of scope (decision/policy, not hazard ID)
grade_crosswalk.notes: Held OUTSIDE the certainty ladder; reported as context only (consistent with all frameworks).

grade_crosswalk.manuscript_definition: Modeled or measured environmental cancer-risk estimate without observed incidence
grade_crosswalk.GRADE_certainty: Very low (modeled, indirect; not observed incidence)
grade_crosswalk.OHAT_confidence_and_hazard: Exposure-assessment stream; not a hazard-ID effect estimate
grade_crosswalk.notes: Risk-assessment output (e.g. EPA AirToxScreen), not an observed-incidence study.

note: A-F labels PRESERVED; this maps them to standard frameworks. IARC is AGENT-level (not study-level) and is context for the 'Established' claim level. Framework citations: see methods_references.bib (UNVERIFIED - confirm; no network in build env).
